title: How an ordinary question becomes a business case you can understand and check
principle: Start with what a person can recognize. Explain the reasoning in ordinary language. Keep every important source, concept, calculation, disagreement, and unknown within reach.

views.label: Whole case
views.title: From something you notice to a question you can test.
views.summary: An Opportunity Case does more than announce a business idea. It shows how the question formed, builds a conditional answer from incomplete evidence, and helps the reader decide what to learn or try next.

steps.title: Something does not quite work
steps.detail: A product is hard to find, a service is slow, a price seems strange, or people keep making an awkward compromise.

steps.title: Turn the observation into a question
steps.detail: Name the people, place, time, alternative, and decision. Explain why this question is useful and which nearby questions were left open.

steps.title: Learn what would have to be true
steps.detail: Follow people, money, work, rules, time, and competing explanations. Introduce each necessary idea where it becomes useful.

steps.title: Give a conditional answer
steps.detail: Say where the case looks promising, where it fails, what remains unknown, and what observation would change the answer.

steps.title: Take the smallest honest next step
steps.detail: Reject the idea, revise it, investigate a decisive unknown, or run the cheapest lawful test before risking more.

views.label: Sources
views.title: A source helps only when you know what it can and cannot show.
views.summary: What people say, buy, avoid, search for, repair, substitute, or tolerate can all matter. None of those signals reveals the whole market or a person's hidden true preference by itself.

steps.title: Show what we encountered
steps.detail: Link the document, price, observation, interview, transaction, or field report. State who produced it, where, when, and under what conditions.

steps.title: Explain why it deserves attention
steps.detail: Say what the source directly knows, how close it is to the event, what incentive shaped it, and why it helps with this question.

steps.title: Name what it leaves out
steps.detail: Look for missing people, changed prices, selection effects, conflicts, local limits, and the difference between words and behaviour.

steps.title: Compare other explanations
steps.detail: Ask what else could produce the same pattern and seek evidence that would distinguish those possibilities.

steps.title: State only what the bundle supports
steps.detail: Keep the observation, interpretation, assumption, and recommendation separate in the explanation, without making the reader learn private labels.

views.label: Ideas
views.title: Explain the idea before asking the reader to use its name.
views.summary: Terms such as incentive, working capital, substitution, or break-even are useful when they help a reader see a relationship—not when they act as passwords into business knowledge.

steps.title: Begin with the familiar situation
steps.detail: Describe what people are choosing, giving up, waiting for, paying for, or risking in language that works without the term.

steps.title: Name the idea
steps.detail: Introduce the shared term so the reader can recognize it elsewhere, then give a short explanation beside it.

steps.title: Show where it came from
steps.detail: Offer a deeper path through the problem people were trying to solve, how the idea changed, and which observations made it useful.

steps.title: Show its limits and disagreements
steps.detail: Explain when the idea stops travelling well, what alternatives exist, and what researchers or practitioners still contest.

steps.title: Return it to this decision
steps.detail: Make clear what the idea helps us notice here and what it cannot decide for the reader.

views.label: Numbers
views.title: Explain the relationship first; show the exact mathematics underneath.
views.summary: Numbers make a case more exact only when a reader can understand what is being represented, why the calculation was chosen, and which uncertain inputs control the result.

steps.title: Say what we are trying to understand
steps.detail: For example: whether cash returns before bills are due, how many sales cover fixed costs, or how a delay changes the amount of money required.

steps.title: Show the pieces in human terms
steps.detail: Connect price, volume, cost, time, interest, loss, and capacity to the real people, work, and events they stand for.

steps.title: Expose the formula and inputs
steps.detail: Keep the exact calculation reproducible. Identify which figures were observed, estimated, assumed, or borrowed from another setting.

steps.title: Let the reader try other worlds
steps.detail: Change the fragile inputs, compare plausible ranges, and show where the result crosses from workable to dangerous.

steps.title: Say what the number cannot prove
steps.detail: A tidy model does not make an uncertain market certain. Name the behaviour, shock, or missing relationship it does not capture.

views.label: Correction
views.title: A challenge should help everyone see the case more clearly.
views.summary: Participation matters when it adds a source, corrects a number, exposes a hidden assumption, supplies local experience, or opens a better question—not when it merely wins agreement.

steps.title: Point to the part in question
steps.detail: Identify the statement, source, concept, assumption, calculation, local comparison, or unanswered question that needs attention.

steps.title: Bring a reason or observation
steps.detail: Add traceable evidence, relevant experience, a counterexample, an alternative calculation, or a real-world test outcome.

steps.title: Work through the disagreement
steps.detail: Explain where the accounts differ, which assumptions create the difference, and what new evidence could resolve it.

steps.title: Revise without erasing
steps.detail: Update the public case while keeping what changed, why it changed, and what remains disputed visible to later readers.

views.label: What remains
views.title: The result is a better decision and a more capable reader.
views.summary: A case succeeds when it prevents waste, improves a test, or clarifies a real choice—and when the reader can carry its questions and ways of checking into another situation.

steps.title: Understand this opportunity
steps.detail: The reader can explain the people, gap, alternatives, economics, practical work, important evidence, and decisive uncertainty in their own words.

steps.title: See how the answer was built
steps.detail: Sources, concepts, calculations, assumptions, disagreements, and unknowns remain connected to the conclusion instead of disappearing behind it.

steps.title: Choose without borrowed certainty
steps.detail: Reject, adapt, keep learning, or test the idea while understanding what the research does and does not justify.

steps.title: Ask a better next question
steps.detail: The reader leaves with language, source paths, and habits of inquiry that remain useful beyond this one case.

steps.title: Let reality teach us again
steps.detail: Outcomes return to the case so readers can compare what happened with what people believed and improve the shared understanding.
